plotSections.title: The Journal and the Mother's Prayer
bullets: Sylan reveals that a relatively recent handwritten journal, written by multiple hands over time, described the Navi searching for a surviving child whose mother had died.
The journal also contained a plot concerning the murder of Sylan's family that later occurred, but Sylan says it was not Nevarr's tome and that he does not remember any explicit prophecy within it.
A meditation in Jotunheim revealed to Sylan that the child described in the journal was Gerk and that Gerk was apparently a keeper who would open doors.

Dana recalls the prophecy repeatedly heard in the stronghold, describing a gate opening, eight being torn asunder, dormant keys, arches as doors, and a mysterious burden. This prophecy is identified as the Mother's Prayer.
Plymouth Gawater and Kit Anger become significantly more attentive when Sylan connects Gerk to the journal, the Navi, and the Mother's Prayer.

plotSections.title: Gerk and the Mother's Prayer
bullets: Gerk is confirmed as the child foretold by the Mother's Prayer and as a potential keeper who will open doors, although the prophecy does not dictate his choices or explain exactly how he arrived at his current circumstances.
The Mother's Prayer is an ancient sacred prophecy of the Navi that describes a recurring pattern of catastrophe, a hero emerging from it, and that hero eventually facing difficult choices.
The prophecy has been recorded in multiple journals or tomes by different authors and can apparently change or rewrite itself when a son or daughter of the Great Tree chooses a different path.

The Mother's Prayer is described through a tree-and-fruit metaphor: the prophecy is the tree and its chosen heroes are the fruit produced by it. The Great Tree has diminished over time and is approaching another growth cycle.

Plymouth explains that Gerk is one of the sons and daughters of the Great Tree and is the first such individual in roughly 1,500 years to step forward and potentially accept the role described by the Mother's Prayer.
Plymouth says he has previously communicated with three other sons or daughters of the Great Tree; one accepted the challenge, while the other two apparently did not continue with it.

Gerk is offered a choice between rejecting the role and effectively falling from the tree, or accepting guidance and being plucked from the tree to fulfill the role. Gerk agrees to proceed if doing so will help Atlas.

Gerk's choice affects his companions because the Mother's Prayer includes stipulations concerning the camaraderie of the chosen child and his friends. The companions may voluntarily join him, while Gerk's decision takes precedence.
Dana immediately chooses to follow Gerk, stating that if he has been chosen there must be a purpose and that she will go wherever he goes. Walker, Sylan, Ord, and Ciri also ultimately step forward.

Gerk asks about Daisy, the mysterious girl associated with flowers. He says she has previously stopped time without anyone else noticing, but the DM cannot yet identify her and says he will need to investigate his notes.

plotSections.title: The Eldarin Tree and the Children of the Tree
bullets: Plymouth Gawater explains that the Eldarin Tree is an ancient and sacred tree of the Navi and one of the most significant magical places in Atlas.
The Eldarin Tree has rings analogous to the rings of Atlas. The Navi studied and distilled knowledge from those rings, eventually creating the keystones.

The creation of the keystones unintentionally set the Mother's Prayer into motion, causing the prophecy to bring forth individuals when Atlas requires them to act for the world's health and prosperity.
Gerk's acceptance of the role is described as being plucked from the Great Tree like ripe fruit, while his companions can join him and become associated with the Tree's other sons and daughters.
The party's acceptance of the role makes them Children of the Great Eldarin Tree and honorary members of the Navi, giving them significant responsibilities connected to the keystones.

plotSections.title: The Doorman and the Gatekeepers
bullets: Plymouth Gawater offers Gerk the title of Doorman, a role that has not been granted in many years.
The Doorman can reach out to an Arch, find an invisible handle, open and close a door through reality, connect with the Arch, and protect it.
Gerk accepts the role and is distinguished from the other party members, who become Gatekeepers responsible for individual keystones and realms.
Unlike previous keepers, who primarily hid and preserved their keystones, the new Gatekeepers are expected to protect, actively use, and improve their associated realms.
The party is warned that the keystones are powerful objects and that the lich they have been trying to find is also seeking them, making their new stewardship particularly dangerous.

plotSections.title: The Keystone Keepers
bullets: Gerk chooses the Keystone of Midgard and becomes its Doorman.
Sylan accepts the Keystone of Gilbrick, with Plymouth noting that Sylan's connection to the lord of that realm gives him a special claim to the choice.
Walker chooses the Keystone of The Reach rather than La-rel. Although La-rel was his former home, Walker feels it represents his past rather than who he is now, and Glimmen supports either choice.
Dana accepts the Keystone of Pitel, described as the center of the rings of Atlas, and becomes its protector.
Ord chooses the Keystone of Feldspar, a realm associated with magic, science, alchemy, and experimentation.
Ciri chooses the Keystone of Lith. Although Lith has officially rejected magic, its people encounter supernatural phenomena through folklore, cryptids, fairy tales, and legends.
The six active keepers are therefore Gerk/Midgard, Sylan/Gilbrick, Dana/Pitel, Walker/The Reach, Ord/Feldspar, and Ciri/Lith.
Eight keystones exist in total. Turof and La-rel remain unclaimed and are temporarily kept under the stewardship of Kit Anger and the Navi until future keepers can take up those mantles.

plotSections.title: Realm Clarifications
bullets: La-rel is essentially the Feywild and was Walker's former home. It is highly magical, and its people are relatively unconcerned with the rest of Atlas.
Turof is described as a smaller cousin of La-rel with a similar magical atmosphere.
The Reach is the largest of the Arches and provides extensive territory to explore, making it particularly suited to Walker and Glimmen.
Feldspar is associated with magic, science, and alchemy.

Lith has sworn off magic, but its people are not simply ignorant of supernatural phenomena; they encounter them indirectly through stories, cryptids, fairy tales, and unexplained glimpses of other worlds.

plotSections.title: Gerk's Doorman Power
bullets: Gerk discovers that his Doorman ability allows him to open an invisible door by reaching forward, finding an unseen handle, and pulling it open.
The resulting doorway does not resemble a conventional portal; reality appears to peel or bend back, revealing the destination seamlessly through a normal-width doorway.
Gerk's first attempt opens onto a beach somewhere on Midgard at sunset, with gulls, salt air, and a sea breeze.
The exact destination cannot initially be selected reliably, and even the DM does not know precisely where the first door leads.

Sylan attempts to use his own keystone to interact with a similar doorway but only briefly senses a connection before it disappears, suggesting that the Gatekeepers' abilities function differently from Gerk's Doorman power.

plotSections.title: The White-Flower Girl
bullets: After Gerk receives the Midgard keystone, a breeze carries white flower petals through the cavern and the mysterious small girl previously associated with Gerk appears in a distant corridor.
The girl floats above the central empty passage rather than walking along either side and leaves a trail of white flowers behind her.
Gerk, Sylan, Walker, and Plymouth can all see her, confirming that Gerk is not imagining her presence.
Gerk recognizes from Plymouth's reaction that Plymouth genuinely acknowledges the girl's presence. Gerk also has a strong perception of her appearance and connection to the flowers.
Gerk wants to follow the flower trail immediately, but Sylan convinces him to finish their current undertaking first and promises that they will search for her afterward.
Plymouth tells Gerk that following the girl is part of Gerk's own journey rather than something Plymouth can resolve for him.
The DM has not yet identified the girl's nature and says he will need to consult his notes. Dana's observations about the unexplained flowers reinforce the girl's apparent connection to Gerk.

plotSections.title: The Two Unclaimed Keystones
bullets: The party is reminded that La-rel and Turof must not be forgotten despite lacking dedicated keepers.
Kit Anger and the Navi will temporarily safeguard those two keystones until future individuals can take up their mantles.

The distinction between Gerk's Doorman role and the other Gatekeepers' roles remains important: Gerk can directly open doors through reality, while the other keepers interact with their keystones and Arches differently.

plotSections.title: Experimenting with the Keystone Doors
bullets: After the council disperses, Gerk experiments with his Doorman ability and discovers that the destination changes between attempts.
One attempt opens onto a gray mountainside during a storm, while another opens onto a dark, quiet forest filled with glowing insects.
Dana suggests that Gerk focus on a familiar destination, such as the Great Hall of the Stronghold, to gain better control over the doors.
Gerk attempts to focus on the Stronghold but instead reaches the forest. Dana recognizes its flora and fauna as resembling the area around Langdale.
Walker recognizes a distinctive old, oddly angled tree from previous travels with his bees, providing stronger evidence that the portal opens somewhere near Langdale.
The party concludes that Gerk may be capable of opening doors to locations throughout Atlas, but precise destination control will require practice or a better understanding of the ability.

plotSections.title: Portal Safety and the Party Regroups
bullets: The DM warns Gerk that closing a portal may make it difficult to reopen a door to the exact same location later, but strongly recommends closing it rather than leaving it unattended.
The warning is reinforced by past incidents in which opened doors allowed dangerous creatures or other unwanted things to pass through.
Walker is eager to use the portal to return home, while Dana and Sylan urge the group not to rush through it.
Sylan points out that the party has just acquired a major responsibility and suggests that they organize themselves and process what they have learned before acting further.
The party winds down with drinks and discusses visiting a tavern after finishing their business; these social plans do not introduce significant new plot information.

plotSections.title: The Gods Depart
bullets: The assembled gods are dismissed after the party's questions. Vecna leaves to find a book, reminds the party that they are still mortal, and encourages them to enjoy their new abilities.
Ben opens a doorway from thin air into his traveling tavern and invites the party to return whenever they wish. Mahali follows him and invites them back to the stronghold for a meal.
Narul, the Stranger, gives the party a quiet farewell before departing.
Emhet reminds the Gatekeepers that they now hold the keys and gives cryptic guidance: if the mind walks, hold your breath, do not yell, trust the path, and trust the gatekeeper.

plotSections.title: The Raven Queen's Counsel
bullets: The Raven Queen approaches the party after the council, initially appearing as a harpy-like figure covered in black feathers before resolving into a slender, regal woman in a dark flowing robe with a blank white porcelain face and owl-like facial features.

She acknowledges that the party has opinions about her and that they have seen and done things she could once have judged them for, but says she understands mortals because she was once more mortal herself and has walked among their world.
She says she has seen some members of the party at the Everfalls, particularly Sylan and Dana, and tells them that they have accomplished more than she expected.

The Raven Queen expresses particular confidence in Sylan, while saying Walker and Ord have not impressed her as greatly but have nevertheless shown her something beyond what she normally sees from mortals.
She offers to lead the party where they need to go but warns them not to turn the journey into a fool's errand or waste her time or theirs.
She warns the party not to treat death casually, explaining that lives and opportunities related to death are finite and that some of them may not have many chances remaining.
The Raven Queen tells the party to make their lives meaningful rather than trying to defy death, emphasizing that they should make their lives and eventual deaths worth remembering.
When Sylan declines to ask her anything further, she tells him to remember where he has been, where he will go, and what he has, and not to throw those things away or live in preparation for death.
She reminds Sylan that he has been given a weapon and is a 'talon' of her order, not a butcher, establishing a specific philosophy for his role.
The Raven Queen ultimately transforms back into her enormous black-winged harpy-like form and flies away.

chronologicalEvents: The party remains in the gods' council while the gods continue their deliberations. Gerk privately asks Sylan whether he should tell Plymouth and the others that Sylan believes Gerk is special and chosen, and Sylan encourages him to trust his instincts. Gerk ultimately decides to reveal it publicly.

Sylan explains that he found a relatively recent handwritten journal written by multiple authors describing the Navi searching for a child whose mother died while the child survived. The journal also described a plot against Sylan's family that eventually happened. Sylan's meditation in Jotunheim revealed that the child was Gerk and that he was a keeper who would open doors.
The DM confirms that Sylan's journal is not Nevarr's tome and asks whether it contains a prophecy. Sylan says he knows of no explicit prophecy in it, while the DM introduces the term Mother's Prayer.

Dana recalls the Mother's Prayer heard echoing through the stronghold, describing gates opening, eight being torn asunder, sleeping keys, arches, and doors waiting to awaken. The prophecy is also referred to as the Mother's Prophecy or Mother's Tale and is connected to the child and keeper described by Sylan.

Kit Anger and Plymouth Gawater take increased interest in Sylan's revelations. Plymouth approaches Gerk and asks whether he believes he is the individual described by the Mother's Prayer. Gerk says he cannot know whether he is the chosen person and that he is simply doing what makes him happy.

Plymouth explains that the Mother's Prayer is an ancient sacred prophecy of the Navi, with an unknown original seer and many versions recorded by different authors. It traditionally involves a catastrophe, a hero, and increasingly difficult choices for that hero.

Plymouth confirms that Gerk is the person spoken of by the prophecy and one of the sons or daughters of the Great Eldarin Tree. He explains that the prophecy does not remove Gerk's agency: Gerk's past choices were his own, and Mother's Tales can rewrite themselves when a child of the Tree chooses a different path.

Plymouth reveals that he has communicated with three other sons or daughters of the Great Tree, but none has taken up the role for approximately 1,500 years. When Gerk questions how they can know the prophecy refers to him, Plymouth points to specific factual information in the prophecy concerning someone close to Gerk as evidence that it is more specific than a generic description.

Gerk agrees to accept the path if doing so can help Atlas. Plymouth and the DM explain that Gerk's acceptance brings the rest of the party into the situation because the chosen child's relationship with his companions carries associated stipulations. The companions may voluntarily join him as metaphorical brothers and sisters of the chosen child.

Walker learns that Gerk is a chosen child of the Great Tree and that the Tree is connected to the Mother's Prayer. Dana states that she will follow Gerk wherever he goes because his selection implies a greater purpose. The party recognizes that Gerk's companions may become connected to the Great Tree through him.

The party discusses Gerk's new status with jokes about crowns and capes, including a joke about making a crown for Glimmen, but Plymouth clarifies that crowns are not part of the Great Tree ceremony. Walker jokes about becoming the Tree's grandfather and then godfather, with Mahali receiving a joking wink.

The party discusses Daisy, the mysterious small girl associated with white flowers. Gerk recalls that Daisy has followed him before and may have stopped time without anyone else noticing. Dana connects unexplained white flowers to Daisy's presence. The DM says Daisy's apparent presence is difficult to explain and that he will need to check his notes; Plymouth clarifies that Daisy is not part of the current Great Tree revelation.
Ciri speaks from the shadows, obscures her location with her voice, and later teleports to Ben before rejoining the party.

The DM calls Dana, Gerk, Walker, Ord, Sylan, and Ciri forward to participate in Gerk's newly offered status or affiliation. The entire party agrees to join Gerk despite not yet knowing all of its responsibilities, with Walker explicitly saying he trusts Gerk. Kit Anger and Juten Prime step back and allow the ceremony to proceed, and the party joins Gerk in the center of the dais.

Gawater explains that Gerk is a son of the Great Tree and identifies the Eldarin Tree as sacred to the Navi. He explains that the Navi created the keystones by studying and distilling knowledge from the rings of the Eldarin Tree, and that creating the keystones unintentionally initiated the Mother's Prayer, a self-propagating prophecy that calls forth individuals when Atlas needs them.

Gawater offers Gerk the long-unused title of Doorman, giving him responsibility and power to open, close, connect with, and protect an Arch. Gerk accepts the role of Doorman, while the other party members become Gatekeepers.

Plymouth retrieves a keystone from the concentric circles and initially presents Gerk with the Keystone of Pitel. The party discusses Pitel, Feldspar, Gilbrick, Lith, Turof, La-rel, the Reach, and Midgard while helping Gerk decide which realm to choose.
Gerk chooses Midgard/Midgar and receives its keystone. The DM explains that previous keepers preserved their realms, while the new keepers must protect, utilize, and improve them.

White flower petals appear as Gerk accepts the Midgard keystone, and the mysterious white-flower girl appears in a distant corridor. Gerk's natural 20 Perception check confirms that Plymouth is genuinely acknowledging the girl's presence. Gerk wants to follow her trail, but Sylan persuades him to wait until the current proceedings are complete.
Sylan accepts the Keystone of Gilbrick as the child of the lord of that realm.

Walker is offered the Keystone of La-rel because he is the only party member not actually from Midgard. He declines La-rel because it represents an important part of his past and instead chooses the Reach because it better reflects who he is now. Glimmen tells Walker that home is where they make it and is willing to accompany him to either realm.
Walker receives the Keystone of the Reach. The Reach is described as the largest Arch, with extensive territory that Walker and Glimmen should be able to traverse efficiently.
Dana is offered the Keystone of Pitel because of her previous interest in reaching Pitel and accepts it, declaring that she is honored to guard the center of the rings of Atlas.

Ord asks about Gilbrick, learns it is already claimed, and chooses Feldspar because of its combination of magic, science, and alchemy. Feldspar is described as a realm involving unusual magical and scientific experimentation.

The DM explains that Lith has culturally rejected magic, but its people are not ignorant and still encounter supernatural phenomena, which they interpret through stories, fairy tales, cryptids, legends, and unexplained glimpses into other worlds. The DM notes that Ord could potentially be regarded as a deity in Lith because of the powers he can bestow.

Ciri returns and is told to choose among the remaining keystones. She is offered La-rel, Turof, or Lith and chooses Lith. The DM explains that Lith's people may call Ciri a witch if she uses magic, but she will nevertheless become part of their history and may eventually have holidays named after her.

La-rel is identified as the realm of fairies, also called the Feywilds, and Renard is recalled as the smiling trickster the party encountered there. The party confirms that they have previously visited La-rel but have not knowingly visited Turof or Lith.

The party confirms that there are eight keystones but only six current keepers. La-rel and Turof remain unchosen, so Kit Anger and the DM's character agree to steward those keystones until future keepers can take up the mantles.

The party is formally recognized as keepers of the keystones, Children of the Great Eldarin Tree, and honorary members of the Navi. Gerk is distinguished as the Doorman while the other party members are Gatekeepers.

The DM points out the irony that the party has been pursuing a lich seeking the keystones while the party has now been entrusted with protecting those same objects. The party is warned that the keystones are powerful and require great care, and the DM begins explaining that Gerk's new mantle makes him more than he was before, though the explanation is not completed in the transcript.

Gerk demonstrates the Doorman ability by reaching for a nonexistent handle and opening an invisible door that bends reality, revealing a beach at sunset somewhere on Midgard. The DM explains that the destination cannot currently be selected precisely and was somewhere on a Midgard coastline.
Sylan attempts to use his keystone to interact with a doorway and briefly senses an invisible opening, but the connection disappears and he cannot yet open it.

The party begins experimenting with Gerk's keystone doors. Gerk opens another portal onto a rainy gray mountainside with distant thunder, then attempts to target the Stronghold but instead opens a portal onto a dark forest illuminated by glowing insects.

Dana recognizes the forest as having flora and fauna consistent with the area around Langdale. Walker investigates using his experience as a wanderer and recognizes a distinctive old, oddly angled tree from a previous journey, confirming that the portal opens somewhere near Langdale.
The party discusses whether to use the portal to return home, but Dana and Sylan argue that they should pause and consider their new responsibilities and finish their remaining business first.
Plymouth gives Dana a bottle after she asks for a drink, and the party discusses the possibility of reaching other places through the portals.

The DM explains that Gerk's currently open portal may be difficult to close and reopen to the exact same location, and strongly advises him to close it because previous incidents have allowed dangerous creatures through open doors.

The assembled gods begin departing after the party concludes its questioning. Walker asks whether there is anything further to learn about Grixto, and Vecna says he needs to find a book before the meeting can fully conclude. Vecna later reminds the party that they remain mortal despite their new powers.

Ben opens a doorway from thin air into his traveling tavern and invites the party to return. Mahali follows and invites them to the stronghold for food. Narul quietly departs after giving the party a farewell.

Emhet prepares to depart and tells the party that they now hold the keys. He gives cryptic instructions concerning mind walking, holding their breath, remaining silent, trusting the path, and trusting the gatekeeper, specifically advising Dana not to yell if the mind walks.

The Raven Queen approaches the party and reveals a regal humanoid appearance beneath her previous harpy-like form. She acknowledges the party's past opinions and actions toward her, says she understands mortals and has been among them before, and says the party has exceeded her expectations.

The Raven Queen offers to guide the party where they need to go while warning them not to waste their time or treat death lightly. She says she is willing to bargain and warns that some members of the party may have few chances or lives remaining. She tells the party not to defy death but to make their lives and eventual deaths something worth remembering.

The Raven Queen asks Sylan whether there is anything else he wants from her. Sylan declines. She tells him to remember what he has, where he has been, and where he is going, warns him not to prepare for death, and identifies him as a talon of her order rather than a butcher.
The Raven Queen departs by transforming into a shadow-cloaked, harpy-like form with enormous black wings and flying away.
The party remains with Glimmen, Juten Prime, Elrus, Araden, Boris, and Kit Anger while winding down the session. Sylan reflects on the Raven Queen's guidance and records notes about the conversation.
The party begins winding down the session, discussing drinks and a possible future tavern visit.

Accepts the responsibility associated with the prophecy because it may help all of Atlas, while maintaining that his choices remain his own.
Becomes the Doorman, a role distinct from the other Gatekeepers that allows him to open, close, connect with, and protect an Arch.
Chooses Midgard as his keystone realm and is expected to actively protect, use, and improve it rather than merely preserve its keystone.
Can open seamless doorways through reality by manipulating an invisible handle. His destinations are currently unpredictable, including a beach, a gray mountainside, and a forest near Langdale.
Is formally welcomed as a Child of the Great Eldarin Tree and an honorary member of the Navi.
Is repeatedly drawn to the mysterious white-flower girl, Daisy, and wants to follow her trail.
Initially remains skeptical of his prophetic importance and prefers traveling and doing what makes him happy with his friends.

newTerms.name: Sylan
notes: Half-elf rogue and Gatekeeper of Gilbrick.
Possesses a relatively recent handwritten journal containing information about the Navi searching for a surviving child whose mother died.
A meditation in Jotunheim revealed to him that Gerk was the child described in the journal and that Gerk was a keeper who would open doors.
Accepts the Gilbrick keystone and becomes its Gatekeeper.
Can sense a connection when attempting to use the Gilbrick keystone but has not yet mastered it.
Is recognized by the Raven Queen as a talon of her order rather than a butcher and receives guidance to value what he has and not prepare himself for death.
Is cautious about revealing information until he understands its significance and tends to reflect carefully on important revelations.

newTerms.name: Sylan's Journal
notes: A relatively recent handwritten journal found and retained by Sylan, apparently written by multiple authors or in multiple hands.
Describes the Navi searching for a surviving child whose mother died.
Also contains a plot against Sylan's family that later occurred.
Sylan does not recall an explicit prophecy in the journal and knows it is distinct from Nevarr's tomes.
Its authorship, connection to the Mother's Prayer, and apparent knowledge of events remain unexplained.

newTerms.name: Navi
notes: Ancient people associated with the Great Eldarin Tree, keystones, and the Mother's Prayer.
Historically sought the children produced through the Mother's Prayer to aid their efforts across Atlas.
Were searching for the surviving child identified by Sylan as Gerk.
The party becomes honorary members of the Navi after accepting the keystone-keeper mantles.

newTerms.name: Jotunheim
notes: Homeland of the Juten/Jotun.
Sylan performed a meditation there that revealed Gerk's identity as the child described in his journal and indicated that Gerk would open doors.

newTerms.name: Mother's Prayer
notes: Also called the Mother's Prophecy, Mother's Tale, or Mother's Tales.
An ancient sacred prophecy or world-level process associated with the early history of the Navi, the Great Eldarin Tree, and Atlas.
Its verses concern gates, keys, arches, catastrophe, a chosen hero, burdens, and difficult choices.
The prophecy is connected to Gerk and has explicitly identified him as its current chosen child.
It appears to call forth individuals when Atlas needs them; its creation was unintentionally initiated when the Navi created the keystones.

The prophecy describes a path without completely determining the chosen individual's decisions, and its accounts can apparently rewrite themselves when a child of the Tree chooses an independent path.
The Great Eldarin Tree is dwindling, and a new bud is expected as the current growing season ends.
Its ultimate origin, mechanism, and the meaning of its references to the eight, keys, arches, and mind remain unclear.

newTerms.name: Kit Anger
notes: NPC who becomes particularly attentive when Sylan discusses the journal, Navi, and Gerk.
Welcomes Gerk as a brother after his recognition as a Child of the Tree.
Will steward the unassigned Turof and La-rel keystones alongside the DM until future keepers take their mantles.

newTerms.name: Plymouth Gawater
notes: Gnome artificer and friend of the party with extensive knowledge of the Great Eldarin Tree, Mother's Prayer, Navi, and keystones.
Recognizes Gerk as the child described by the Mother's Prayer and explains that Gerk's choice is voluntary.
Explains that Gerk's companions can become connected to the chosen child as metaphorical brothers and sisters.
Offers Gerk the title of Doorman and explains its responsibilities.
Explains that the keystones were created by distilling knowledge from the rings of the Great Eldarin Tree and that their creation unintentionally initiated the Mother's Prayer.
Oversees the party's keystone assignments and explains that the new keepers are expected to actively use and protect the keystones.
Can see the mysterious white-flower girl and confirms that her appearance is not merely Gerk's imagination.

newTerms.name: Great Eldarin Tree
notes: Sacred tree associated with the ancient Navi and the origin of the keystones.
Its rings were studied and distilled by the Navi to create the keystones.
The Mother's Prayer metaphorically represents the tree, with chosen individuals appearing as its fruit or children.
Gerk is explicitly identified as a son or child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
The tree has diminished significantly and is described as being in grave circumstances, with a new bud expected at the end of the current growing season.
Taking on the keystone-keeper mantles makes the party Children of the Great Eldarin Tree and honorary members of the Navi.

newTerms.name: Atlas
notes: The world containing the various Arch realms.
The Mother's Prayer and the keystone keepers have significance across Atlas rather than only within a single realm.
Gerk's acceptance of his role is presented as potentially benefiting the health and prosperity of all Atlas.

newTerms.name: Daisy
notes: Mysterious small girl associated with Gerk and recurring appearances around the party.
Associated with unexplained appearances of white flowers and a recurring trail of white flowers.
Gerk claims she has previously stopped time without others noticing.
Gerk, Sylan, Walker, Plymouth, and others can apparently perceive her or evidence of her presence.
Her identity, connection to Gerk and the Great Eldarin Tree, and possible ability to manipulate time remain unexplained.

newTerms.name: Dana
notes: Half-elf cleric and one of the party's most knowledgeable members.
Loyal to Gerk and accepts his chosen status as having a meaningful purpose.
Chooses Pitel and becomes its Gatekeeper, responsible for the center of the rings of Atlas.
Had previously sought a way to reach Pitel, apparently because of its unusual relationship with time.
Recognizes Daisy's flowers as evidence that the mysterious girl was present.
Receives cryptic guidance from Emhet concerning the mind walking and holding her breath.
Advises Gerk to focus on familiar locations to improve control over his doors and urges caution with unstable portals.

newTerms.name: Walker
notes: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter; Glimmen is his mind-linked dragon.
Strongly loyal to Gerk and joins his new path without needing to understand all of its details.
Chooses The Reach rather than his former home of La-rel because The Reach better represents who he is now.
Becomes Gatekeeper of The Reach and is expected to protect and explore the largest Arch.
His travel experience helps identify a portal destination as being near Langdale.
Can see the mysterious white-flower girl and her trail.
Tends to respond to major revelations with humor while remaining willing to accept responsibility.

newTerms.name: Glimmen
notes: Walker's mind-linked dragon.
Supports Walker's choice between La-rel and The Reach and views home as wherever they make it.
Has prior experience with La-rel and is well suited, alongside Walker, to traversing the vast Reach.

newTerms.name: Sitting Stones
notes: A location or magical means Sylan previously used when investigating information connected to the Navi and another person's role.

newTerms.name: Ciri
notes: Half-elf rogue who uses stealth, misdirection, and theatrical entrances.
Joins Gerk's group and accepts the shared responsibility of the chosen child.
Chooses Lith and becomes its Gatekeeper.
Lith rejects magic culturally, so Ciri's magic may cause its inhabitants to interpret her as a witch or supernatural figure.
Is expected to become part of Lith's history and folklore.

newTerms.name: Ord
notes: Dragonborn paladin.
Joins Gerk's group and accepts the shared responsibility surrounding the chosen child.
Chooses Feldspar because of its combination of magic, science, and alchemy.
Becomes Gatekeeper of Feldspar.
The Raven Queen specifically notes that Ord and Walker have shown her something beyond what she normally sees from mortals, though she was less impressed by them than by some others.

newTerms.name: Ben
notes: Minor deity, keeper of the Watchers, and proprietor of the traveling bar.
Can open a doorway from thin air into his traveling tavern.
Ciri deliberately teleports beside him because she knows he is aware of her presence.
Welcomes the party to return to his tavern.

newTerms.name: Mahali
notes: Elder god and the party's chef.
Responds with amusement to Walker's joke about him being a possible godfather figure.
Invites the party back to the stronghold and offers a meal.

newTerms.name: Raven Queen
notes: Also known as Nira; elder god and goddess of the dead.
Appears in a regal humanoid form wearing a dark robe and blank white porcelain mask, but can transform into a harpy-like figure with enormous black wings.
Has personally walked among mortals and has seen members of the party, including Sylan and Dana, at the Everfalls.
Offers to guide the party when useful but expects them not to waste her time or treat death carelessly.
Encourages the party to live meaningfully rather than trying to defy or prepare for death.
Identifies Sylan as a talon of her order and advises him to remember where he has been, where he will go, and what he has.
Her reasons for knowing about the party and the meaning of some of her warnings remain unclear.

newTerms.name: Vecna
notes: Elder god and god of liches.
Reminds the party that despite their new powers and responsibilities, they remain mortal.
Leaves the gathering to find a book.

newTerms.name: Juten Prime
notes: One of the original or former keepers of the keystones.
Had discussed with Plymouth what would happen if one of Mother's children appeared.
The appearance of one of Mother's children was expected to override prior preparations and require events to take their course.

newTerms.name: Pitel
notes: One of the Arch realms of Atlas.
Described as the center or core of the rings of Atlas and associated with an unusual relationship to time.
Dana receives its keystone and becomes its Gatekeeper.

newTerms.name: Feldspar
notes: One of the Arch realms of Atlas.
A realm focused on knowledge, magic, science, alchemy, and experimentation.
Ord receives its keystone and becomes its Gatekeeper.

newTerms.name: Gilbrick
notes: One of the Arch realms of Atlas.
Sylan receives its keystone and becomes its Gatekeeper because he is considered a child of the lord of Gilbrick.
Gerk does not want to choose Gilbrick, and it is unavailable once Sylan claims it.

newTerms.name: Lith
notes: One of the Arch realms of Atlas and the realm protected by Ciri.
Its people have culturally rejected magic, treating supernatural phenomena through folklore, fairy tales, and cryptid stories.
Magic nevertheless exists, and incursions or gaps involving other worlds can produce local legends.
Ciri's magic may cause her to be remembered as a witch or supernatural figure.

newTerms.name: Keystones
notes: Magical stones corresponding to the eight Arches of Atlas and used to open or interact with paths between realms.
The Navi created them by distilling knowledge from the rings of the Great Eldarin Tree.
Their creation unintentionally initiated the Mother's Prayer.
Six of the eight are currently assigned to party members: Gerk/Midgard, Sylan/Gilbrick, Dana/Pitel, Walker/The Reach, Ord/Feldspar, and Ciri/Lith.
The La-rel and Turof keystones remain unassigned and are being stewarded.

newTerms.name: La-rel
notes: An Arch realm of Atlas with a Feywild-like, highly magical environment and Walker's former home.
Walker declines its keystone because he no longer considers it representative of who he is.
Its keystone remains unassigned and is stewarded by Kit Anger and the DM.
The party has previously visited La-rel and encountered Renard, the smiling trickster.

newTerms.name: Midgard
notes: One of the Arch realms of Atlas.
Gerk chooses its keystone and becomes its keeper.
Gerk is expected to protect, actively use, and help make Midgard greater rather than merely hide its keystone.

newTerms.name: White-Flower Girl
notes: The mysterious girl known to Gerk as Daisy, associated with recurring appearances and trails of white flowers.
She has appeared floating through corridors rather than walking normally.
Several party members can perceive her or evidence of her presence.
Gerk intends to follow her trail, but her identity, destination, and connection to the larger prophecy remain unknown.

newTerms.name: Mother's Children
notes: Designation for individuals brought forth through the Mother's Prayer and connected to the Great Eldarin Tree.
The appearance of one of Mother's children can override prior plans and require events to proceed according to the Mother's process.
Gerk is explicitly identified as one of Mother's children.

newTerms.name: The Reach
notes: The largest Arch realm of Atlas.
Walker chooses its keystone and becomes its Gatekeeper.
Walker believes it better represents his current identity than his former home of La-rel.
Its immense size makes it suited to extensive exploration, particularly for Walker and Glimmen.

newTerms.name: Turof
notes: An Arch realm of Atlas with a magical atmosphere similar to La-rel.
The party has not knowingly visited it.
Its keystone remains unassigned and is stewarded by Kit Anger and the DM.

newTerms.name: Renard
notes: The smiling trickster associated with La-rel.
The party encountered Renard during a previous visit to La-rel.

newTerms.name: Keystone Keepers
notes: The six party members who currently hold and protect individual keystones.
Current assignments are Gerk/Midgard, Sylan/Gilbrick, Dana/Pitel, Walker/The Reach, Ord/Feldspar, and Ciri/Lith.
They are responsible for protecting and responsibly using their keystones and realms.
The party's new responsibilities connect directly to the larger threat because the lich being pursued is also seeking the keystones.
The keepers are recognized as Children of the Great Eldarin Tree and honorary members of the Navi.

newTerms.name: Doorman
notes: Gerk's unique role, distinct from the Gatekeeper role held by the other keystone keepers.
Allows Gerk to open and close an Arch and create seamless doorways directly through reality.
Gerk can manipulate an invisible handle to create a doorway, but its destination is currently unreliable.
The role includes connecting with and protecting the associated Arch.
The full extent of the Doorman's abilities and how destination control works remain unknown.

newTerms.name: Emhet
notes: A deity present at the council who tells the party that they now hold the keys.
Gives cryptic guidance to trust the path and the Gatekeeper.
Warns Dana that if the mind walks, she should hold her breath and not yell.
The meaning of the mind-walking instruction and the referenced path remains unclear.

newTerms.name: Narul
notes: Also known as the Stranger; elder god and former god of death.
Silently acknowledges the party with a nod, forehead gesture, and slight bow before departing.

newTerms.name: Child of the Tree
notes: A designation for an individual connected to the Great Eldarin Tree through the Mother's Prayer.
Gerk is explicitly recognized as a Child of the Tree.
The designation carries a connection to the Navi and the keystone-keeper tradition.

newTerms.name: Gatekeeper
notes: The role held by the party members other than Gerk who receive keystones.
Gatekeepers hold and protect their assigned keystones and interact with the paths between realms.
Current Gatekeepers are Sylan/Gilbrick, Dana/Pitel, Walker/The Reach, Ord/Feldspar, and Ciri/Lith.
The role is explicitly distinguished from Gerk's Doorman role.

newTerms.name: Everfalls
notes: A location from the party's past that the Raven Queen says she has seen Sylan and Dana at.
No further details about what occurred there are established in this material.

newTerms.name: Mind Walk
notes: An unexplained phenomenon referenced by Emhet in instructions to hold one's breath and not yell if the mind walks.
Appears to be connected to traveling through a path or gate.

newTerms.name: Talon
notes: A role or agent of the Raven Queen's order.
Sylan is explicitly identified as a talon.
The role is contrasted with being a butcher, implying purposeful action rather than indiscriminate killing.
Its full duties and abilities remain unknown.

newTerms.name: Stronghold
notes: A party location containing the Great Hall.
Dana suggests that the Great Hall could serve as a familiar destination for Gerk to focus on when attempting to control his portal destinations.

newTerms.name: Boris
notes: An NPC briefly mentioned as being present with the party alongside Glimmen, Juten Prime, Elrus, Araden, and Kit Anger.

newTerms.name: Langdale
notes: Region considered home by the party.
A forest reached through Gerk's portal is identified as being near Langdale.
Dana recognizes its flora and fauna, while Walker recognizes a distinctive tree from previous travels, confirming the region.
